channel.description: Latest articles from The Shawnee News-Star (news-star.com)

item.title: Letter to the editor
item.description: 'Any need met can be called consequential' Dear editor, Cuts in the One Big Beautiful Bill and by DOGE likely will generate some savings at the federal level, but the costs targeted by the cuts haven’t disappeared. The needs behind them still exist, now pushed onto the states.

item.title: The root of the problem: How to navigate Feline Chronic Gingivostomatitis
item.description: While an animal’s immune system is important for protecting them from bacteria, viruses, and other forms of disease, it can sometimes go overboard. In these cases, the immune system can destroy vital cells, like red blood cells and platelets.

item.title: Everyday Home: Safer spending with digital wallets
item.description: Digital wallets can protect your money, keeping it safer than cash or debit cards alone. In this article we will cover what a digital wallet is, how it can make purchasing more convenient, and how it can safeguard your money.

item.title: Shawnee girls' swimming team finishes fourth at Class 5A State Meet
item.description: EDMOND – The Shawnee High School girls’ swimming team claimed fourth place in the Class 5A State Championships on Saturday.

item.title: March happenings at the zoo
item.description: Spring Break is just around the corner; these are some of the events for March at the Oklahoma City Zoo. STARTING FRIDAY, MARCH 6: OKC ZOO’S DINOSAUR EXPEDITION PRESENTED BY MATHIS HOME Get ready to travel through time with the new Dinosaur Expedition, presented by Mathis Home, at the Oklahoma City Zoo and Botanical Garden.

item.title: City Commission denies rezone proposal for abandoned nursing home site
item.description: After being deferred in January, a rezone request regarding a former nursing home long abandoned at 1402 E. Independence was denied at the February Shawnee City Commission meeting. The site sits across the street from Sequoyah Elementary School.

item.title: Community Renewal announces CRMA Music Awards
item.description: Community Renewal of Pottawatomie County is turning up the volume for its 10-year anniversary with the debut of the Community Renewal Music Awards (CRMA) presented by BancFirst, a show-stopping addition to its annual We Care-aoke fundraiser, taking place March 7 at The Grand Event Center in Shawnee. Themed CRMAs, this year’s event promises an unforgettable evening of karaoke, laughter and local star power, all while honoring a decade of connection, compassion and community impact.

item.title: Pottawatomie County Junior Livestock show begins Tuesday
item.description: The annual Pottawatomie County Junior Livestock Show kicks off today at the Expo Center.

item.title: McLoud takes care of business by sweeping district from Tecumseh
item.description: McLOUD - Both Tecumseh teams took early leads over McLoud, but both gave up big runs that allowed McLoud to take two easy wins.
